q: How do I count a second-hand machine in Scope 3 capital goods?
title: Second-hand machines in Scope 3
short: Category 2 asks for the cradle-to-gate emissions of capital goods you buy. A used machine's manufacturing emissions happened when it was first made, so many companies count only refurbishment, parts and transport, and state that choice. Use the same rule every year.
audience: Factories buying used or refurbished equipment

ul: Refurbishment and new parts, from the seller's invoice.
A note that the machine is second-hand and how you treated it.

sections.h: If a buyer or verifier asks
p: Show the purchase invoice, the refurbishment breakdown and your written rule. Consistency matters more than the choice.

senseible: Senseible keeps each bill and invoice behind every figure, dated and fingerprinted, so a reviewer can trace a number back to the document it came from.
